Régie de Distribution d’Eau (REGIDESO).desc: The state water company of the Democratic Republic of Congo, wholly owned by the Congolese state and supervised by the ministries of Energy and Water Resources and of Portfolio. It began in 1939 as a combined water and electricity board, became a limited company in 2014, and had 695,303 subscribers and about 4,613 permanent staff at the end of 2022.

Office de Voirie et Drainage (OVD).desc: A Congolese public body inside the Ministry of Infrastructure, Public Works and Reconstruction that builds and maintains urban roads and roadside drainage across the country. It manages 89 percent of the paved roads in Kinshasa.

sources.title: Etude du plan directeur de transport urbain de Kinshasa

Ministerio de Ambiente, Vivienda y Desar.desc: A Colombian government ministry that until 2011 handled both environment and housing, water and land-use policy. Law 1444 of 2011 split off its housing, land-use and water and sanitation duties to a new Ministry of Housing, City and Territory and renamed the rest the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development.

sources.title: Decreto 3570 de 2011
sources.publisher: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible, Colombia

Fondo Financiero de Proyectos de Desarro.desc: A Colombian state-owned financial body that prepares and manages public development projects for national and local government. Decree 495 of 2019 renamed it Empresa Nacional Promotora del Desarrollo Territorial (ENTerritorio); it is an industrial and commercial state enterprise of a financial character, attached to the National Planning Department and supervised by the financial regulator.

Aguas de La Guajira S.A. E.S.P..desc: A joint-stock utility company that ran the drinking water and sewerage service in Riohacha, Colombia, from the start of the 2000s. Its majority shares were sold on 13 September 2014 and it was renamed Avanzadas Soluciones de Acueducto y Alcantarillado S.A. E.S.P. (ASAA).

sources.title: Evaluación integral de prestadores: Avanzadas Soluciones de Acueducto y Alcantarillado S.A. E.S.P. (Riohacha)
sources.publisher: Superintendencia de Servicios Públicos Domiciliarios, Colombia

Agence Djiboutienne d'Execution des Trav.desc: A Djiboutian state agency that carried out public-interest construction works and community projects, and supported small income-generating activities through micro-credit. It no longer exists on its own: it was merged with the Social Development Fund to form the Agence Djiboutienne de Développement Social, a public administrative body set up by decree in 2008 under the State Secretariat for Solidarity.

sources.title: Djibouti Social Development Agency: fusion of FSD and ADETIP

Instituto Nacional de Recursos Hidráulic.desc: The Dominican Republic's national water agency, created as an autonomous state body by Law No. 6 of 1965 and based in Santo Domingo. It plans and builds river works, dams, irrigation systems and hydroelectric plants, runs the national irrigation systems, and assesses the country's water resources.

sources.title: Ley No. 6 que crea el Instituto Nacional de Recursos Hidráulicos

Empresa Pública Aguas de Manta (EPAM).desc: The municipal water company of Manta, Ecuador, set up by the city council in 2010 and owned by the Manta municipal government, whose mayor chairs its board. It supplies drinking water and runs the sewerage, stormwater and wastewater treatment systems for the canton; a 2020 ordinance kept the same company and gave it a longer formal name.

sources.title: Ordenanza 023-2020 sustitutiva de creación de la EP Aguas de Manta
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del Cantón Manta

Municipal Development Fund of Georgia (M.desc: A Georgian state body, set up in 1997 as a legal entity under public law, whose work is coordinated by the Ministry of Infrastructure. It lends to and invests in local government infrastructure, including water and sewerage systems, schools, housing for displaced people, and works at tourism and cultural heritage sites.

National Agency for Cultural Heritage Pr.desc: A Georgian state agency set up by presidential decree in 2008 to protect and promote the country's monuments and heritage sites. It keeps the national register and inventory of monuments, documents intangible heritage, advises on restoration, and runs a group of museum-reserves including Vardzia, Uplistsikhe and Gremi.

sources.title: Georgia national policy report: organisations (HEREIN European Heritage Network)

Roads Department of Georgia.desc: The Georgian state body that designs, builds and maintains the country's international and intrastate roads under the Law on Roads of 1994, with the Ministry of Infrastructure setting policy and hearing appeals against its decisions. A 2023 presentation by the department put the network in its care at 6,970 km, of which 1,511 km are international roads, and its staff at 238; municipalities keep the local roads.

sources.title: Law of Georgia on Roads (No. 585, 1994, consolidated)
Roads Department of Georgia: vision presentation

Lands Commission, Ghana.desc: Ghana's national land administration body, established by Article 258 of the 1992 Constitution and remodelled by the Lands Commission Act, 2008 (Act 767). It manages public land and land vested in the President, registers deeds and land instruments, regulates surveying and mapping, and provides land valuation, through four divisions.

Ministry of Information and Communicatio.desc: A Gambian government ministry responsible for communications and information technology policy. It took that name in 2011, when the Ministry of Communications, Information and Information Technology was renamed, and in 2022 it was split into the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy and the Ministry of Information.

sources.title: MOCDE Infographic
sources.publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy, The Gambia

Gambia Telecommunications Company Limite.desc: The Gambia's state telecoms operator, incorporated under the country's companies law, with 99 percent of its shares held by the Government of The Gambia and 1 percent by the Gambia Ports Authority. It provides landline voice service and data services including fibre and ADSL, and reported revenue of 455 million dalasi and a loss of 245 million dalasi in 2022, with 1,046 permanent staff at the end of 2017.

sources.title: Performance Audit Report on Service Delivery by Gamtel

Secretaría de Infraestructura y Servicio.desc: A Honduran government ministry responsible for policy on housing, public works, the road, urban and transport systems, public enterprises and the public works concession regime. Its powers were restated by Legislative Decree 266-2013, the law on streamlining public administration.

Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi JSC.desc: A Mongolian coal mining company that holds four of the five licences over the Tavan Tolgoi coking coal deposit. The state holding company Erdenes Mongol owns 65.2 percent of it, about 14.8 percent of its shares were handed to every Mongolian citizen, and 20 percent is unallocated pending a planned share offering; it reported revenue of 1,194 billion tugrik and 717 permanent staff in 2017.

sources.title: Wild Growth: An Assessment of Erdenes Mongol

Agency for State Roads.desc: The North Macedonian state body for the national road network, created in July 2008 by amendments to the Law on Public Roads as successor to the Fund for National and Regional Roads, which had run the network since 1996. A law of 27 December 2012 replaced it with the Public Enterprise for State Roads, which took over its staff, assets and archives.

sources.title: History
sources.publisher: Public Enterprise for State Roads, North Macedonia

Fundación MANA.note: Searched for a foundation of this name linked to La Guajira or Riohacha; the only sources found were about other bodies (the Antioquia MANA food-security programme and unrelated Riohacha organisations). No register entry, foundation website or news page naming Fundación MANA could be opened, so nothing can be said about it.

SAL Consult Limited.note: Only third-party aggregator listings (Devex, DevelopmentAid, ZoomInfo) came up for this name; no company website, company register entry or news page describing SAL Consult Limited could be opened, so its sector, ownership and size are unverified.

Royal Caribbean.desc: A cruise holiday company listed on the New York Stock Exchange as RCL, which owns the Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea Cruises brands and half of a joint venture running TUI Cruises and Hapag-Lloyd Cruises. It operated 66 ships and reported total revenue of 16.5 billion dollars and net income of 2.9 billion dollars for 2024.

sources.title: Royal Caribbean Group Reports 2024 Results (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)

Council for Development and Reconstructi.desc: A Lebanese public institution created by legislative decree No. 5 of 31 January 1977 and answering directly to the Council of Ministers. It draws up national development and reconstruction plans, runs the projects, and may take domestic and foreign loans; it reported about 10.9 billion dollars of projects carried out or under way between 1992 and 2016.

sources.title: CDR after 40 years: USD 11 billion of projects

Administracao de Infra-estruturas de Agu.desc: A Mozambican state body created by Decree 19/2009 to manage public water supply and wastewater and stormwater drainage systems. It is a Category A public institute with its own legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, overseen by the authority for water supply and sanitation and, on finance, by the finance minister; it was restructured by Decree 112/2020.

Companhia dos Caminhos de Ferro da Beira.desc: A railway concession company set up to rehabilitate and run Mozambique's Beira rail corridor, including the 317 km line from Beira to the Zimbabwe border and the Sena line to the Moatize coal mines, under a 25-year concession. At the 2004 award the Indian state firms RITES and IRCON held 26 and 25 percent and the Mozambican state railway CFM held 49 percent.

sources.title: RITES-IRCON consortium takes over Beira rail corridor in Mozambique
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

Directorate General of Highways, Ministr.desc: The arm of Indonesia's Ministry of Public Works and Housing that builds and maintains national roads and bridges, working through regional road implementation units. It reported 47,603 km of national roads in the first half of 2023.

sources.title: Buku Kondisi Jalan Nasional 2023 Semester I
sources.publisher: Direktorat Jenderal Bina Marga, Kementerian PUPR, Indonesia

Ministry of Public Works and Transport,.desc: One of the government ministries of Lesotho. The country's Roads Directorate began as a department inside this ministry and was made a separate corporate body by the Roads Directorate Act of 2010.

Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Jor.desc: The Jordanian government ministry for tourism and for the country's archaeological heritage. Tourism was first handled by a bureau from 1953, was raised to a ministry by royal decree in 1967, and the ministry took its present name in 1989, when the Department of Antiquities was brought under it.

sources.title: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities: General Information

Customs Administration.desc: North Macedonia's customs service, founded on 14 April 1992 under the Law on the Customs Administration. It is a body within the Ministry of Finance with its own legal personality, clears and inspects imported goods, and is the country's sole administrator of excise duties; it collected 131,634.3 million denars, about 2.14 billion euro, in 2025.

sources.title: Our Role
sources.publisher: Customs Administration of the Republic of North Macedonia

sources.title: Annual Report 2025
sources.publisher: Customs Administration of the Republic of North Macedonia

Ahwaz Water and Wastewater Company.note: No page naming this exact company could be opened. Its own site refused automated access, and the available Iranian and international reports name the Khuzestan Water and Wastewater Company, a provincial body, rather than an Ahwaz company, so describing that one would mean describing a different entity.

State Commission for Roads and Bridges,.note: Iraqi official tender notices and World Bank project documents for the same ministry name a Roads and Bridges Directorate (دائرة الطرق والجسور) as the body that owns and procures road and bridge works, not a State Commission; the abbreviation SCRB appears only in a project engineer's email address. No page naming a State Commission for Roads and Bridges and setting out what it is could be opened, so the exact entity is unconfirmed.

Smith Warner International.desc: A coastal engineering and shoreline management consultancy founded in 1995 by David Smith and Philip Warner, based in Kingston, Jamaica, with offices in St Lucia, Trinidad and Tobago and Vancouver. Its site says it has 30 full-time professional staff and shows projects in nine Caribbean countries and territories.

Mirai Construction Company Limited.note: No company website, company register entry, tender award page or news report naming Mirai Construction Company Limited could be opened; searches of Saint Lucian and regional construction listings returned only generic directory pages with no entry for it, so its sector, ownership and size are unverified.

China First.note: The name on its own does not identify a company that can be checked: searches turned up several unrelated firms with 'China First' in their names, such as China First Highway Engineering Co. Ltd, and no page could be opened that names a contractor simply called 'China First' or describes it. Describing any of the longer-named firms would risk describing the wrong entity.

Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCoP).note: No decree, ministry page or project document naming a 'Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCoP)' inside the Congolese Ministry of Planning could be opened. The Congolese project units found in searches carry other names (for example the Ministry of Planning's Unité de Coordination et de Management des Projets, UCM, and REGIDESO's Cellule d'Exécution des Projets Eau), and describing one of those would mean describing a different body.

Commission Nationale des Travaux d'Intér.desc: A Gabonese public body with a permanent secretariat that houses and runs the coordination units for donor-financed public works and development projects. A 2021 notice places it under the Ministry of the Economy and Recovery, and it also trains Gabonese small and medium firms in World Bank procurement rules.

sources.title: Avis de recrutement, Projet de développement de la statistique (CN-TIPPEE)
Marchés publics: la CNTIPPEE arme les PME gabonaises pour mieux accéder aux financements de la Banque mondiale

Departamento de La Guajira.desc: One of Colombia's departments, the country's regional tier of government, made up of 15 municipalities including Riohacha, Maicao and Uribia. The national statistics office projected its population at 1,002,394 for 2022, based on the 2018 census.

sources.title: InfoDane: Riohacha, La Guajira
sources.publisher: Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística (DANE), Colombia

Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Munici.desc: The municipal government of the canton of Manta, Ecuador, whose powers under the country's local government code (COOTAD) include local planning and land use, water supply and sewerage, waste collection, traffic and transport, urban works, and risk management. The 2022 national census counted 258,697 people in the canton.

sources.title: Informe de gestión GAD Manta 2024
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del Cantón Manta

Housing Fund of the Ministry of Urban De.desc: A Djiboutian state housing body (Fonds de l'Habitat) that is one of two arms carrying out the housing policy of the ministry responsible for housing and urban planning, alongside the Société Immobilière de Djibouti. It has mainly built homes for lower-income households and prepared serviced plots for low-cost housing, and was being relaunched as the Agency for Urban Rehabilitation and Social Housing.

sources.title: Home improvement: the provision of housing remains a critical component of development plans (The Report: Djibouti 2018)

Hanson – Rodríguez, S.R.L..note: No company register entry, company website, state contract award page or news report naming Hanson – Rodríguez, S.R.L. could be opened; Dominican construction searches returned only unrelated firms, so its business, ownership and size are unverified.

Unité Centrale d'Exécution, Ministère de.desc: The central project execution unit of Haiti's Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications. It acts as the implementing agency for the ministry's donor-financed road, drainage and airport projects, running the tenders and contracts.

sources.title: Avis d'appel d'offres: travaux d'assainissement de la ville du Cap-Haïtien (projet RUTAP)

Comité Permanent d'Acquisitions à l'Amia.desc: The Haitian state body that handles expropriations, sitting at the Ministry of Economy and Finance and working with the tax directorate. It identifies affected landholders, checks property titles and values land and buildings against a price framework, then pays; it grew out of the Comité d'Évaluation, which had operated since 1994.

sources.title: Cadre de politique de réinstallation, Haiti Digital Acceleration Project (P171976)

Commissioner of Revenue Administration,.desc: The head office of the revenue arm of the government of Tamil Nadu in India, created in 1980 when the Board of Revenue was abolished and its work split among new commissionerates. Through district collectors and village-level staff it keeps land records and handles mutations, issues certificates such as community, income and legal heirship certificates, acts as custodian of government property, and leads disaster response.

sources.title: Mission
sources.publisher: Commissionerate of Revenue Administration and Disaster Management, Government of Tamil Nadu

Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,.desc: The Ghanaian government ministry whose stated mission is the sustainable management and use of the country's lands, forests, wildlife and mineral resources. It works through three sub-sectors and oversees bodies including the Lands Commission, the Forestry Commission, the Minerals Commission, the Ghana Geological Survey Authority and the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands.

sources.title: Our Ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Ghana

sources.title: Lands Commission (agency page)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Ghana

Ministry of Finance of Mongolia.desc: Mongolia's government ministry for public finance, acting as the central administrative body in charge of finance and budget. Under the Law on Debt Management it draws up the medium-term government debt management strategy alongside the fiscal framework; it reported total government debt of 33,384.6 billion tugrik, or 41.8 percent of GDP, at the end of 2024.
